For years, we’ve scaled intelligence by training larger models and giving them more time to think. But there’s another dimension: running many agents in parallel, exploring different approaches, challenging each other, and working together on solutions that no single agent could easily discover.

the fact that nobody with decisionmaking power saw this coming a mile away and vetoed the 6.2 astra ad is my primary critique of the astra launch

the model itself is solid minor version improvement guys, efficiency is one of the three most impt RL objectives rn and they are world leading here!!! i am daily driving astra and it is the best workflow automation model i’ve used, no longer getting stuck in horrible loops and efficiently learning thru compactions and skill writing. it’s running a lot of our content publishing pipeline for @latentspacepod and @aiDotEngineer and we wouldnt have nearly the revenue efficiency (>1m/employee) that we have as a bootstrapped business without it

technical details:

> inter-session context is surfaced by default. Teams now create dedicated bots for different projects; while these different devins can talk to each other when necessary, they each have their own individual memory bank and goals. Each bot now has its own, long lived identity.  The transition from "Devin is a swarm of ephemeral agents" to "Devin is a collection of bots, each with their own persistent identity and memory" is changing how people use and prompt Devin.

https://t.co/maw20vdPs8

devin bots are multi-agent teams done right:
- always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI)
- own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others)
- manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself)
- available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction)
- consistent reporting thru interactive artifacts aka devinapps not long chats (HTML is all you need™ @trq212)

this is the preview that @walden_yan gave at AIE. i've been trialing them for a week and i've been able to hand over my AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin automation, and video editing work (also simultaneously moving from local agent worktree hell to cloud because ofc this is all cloud based thank god)

hyped concepts this replaces:
- /goal
- "ultracode" / "ultra mode"
- "loop engineering"
- "agent to agent"
- "agent swarms"
- AI employees (see below)

my main aha moment is that you don't want "AI Employees", we do not have agi yet and you will just fail if you overpromise/overexpect. what you want is the "just" the next level of abstraction above single tasks, and the overwhelming consensus I've had talking to everyone at the frontier of agents (yes incl cog competitors) is agent managers that own outcomes. 

incidentally, as an employer of humans it's also how i distinguish between someone who "has agency" (owns a problem area, finds issues and researches/brings solutions not problems) and who doesn't (only does precisely what i asked, not proactive, doesn't come up with suggestions i didn't think about). guess which one i value more lol.

今年 3 月，美国检方曾起诉 3 名 SMCI 相关人员，指控其通过东南亚空壳公司向中国客户非法出售至少 25 亿美元的搭载英伟达 GPU 的服务器。此后，针对 SMCI 的集体诉讼也提及 Cenly Chen 曾负责相关 GPU 采购及客户分配。

不过，Muddy Waters 同时强调，目前没有名为 Cenly Chen 的人士遭到政府起诉或刑事指控，集体诉讼中的相关指控也尚未得到证实。此次做空的核心之一，是对 Puri 与 Chen 身份关联及潜在关系提出质疑，尚不构成已证实的违法证据。

政客不会停止印钞，比特币就不会失去长期上涨的逻辑。

近日，知名比特币投资人 Anthony Pompliano @APompliano 做客 The Iced Coffee Hour，与 Graham Stephan、Jack Selby 讨论比特币、AI 与未来十年的投资机会。

Pomp 的核心观点很直接：只要政府持续印钞，比特币长期就有上涨空间。 比特币不需要不断寻找新的叙事，只要网络持续运行，其稀缺性就会成为长期价值支撑。

访谈涉及几个值得关注的话题：

- 现在入场买比特币是否太晚？
- AI 的崛起会不会让比特币失去吸引力？
- 比特币归零的可能性有多大？
- Graham Stephan 为什么后悔买入狗狗币？
- 将个人财务交给 AI 管理是否安全？

在 AI 热潮不断吸引资金的当下，Pomp 仍然坚定看好比特币，但也坦言，未来的回报率可能不及过去几个周期。

英伟达电话会：董事会无意请回黄仁勋，2028财年营收增速预期上调至75%

英伟达交出超预期财报的同时，管理层释放了更激进的增长预期。

临时 CEO Colette Kress 将 2028 财年营收增速预期从约 70% 上调至 75%，且基于更高的 2027 财年营收基数。第三季度数据中心营收达 1076 亿美元，同比增长 110%；总营收 1158 亿美元，同比增长 103%。Vera Rubin 首个量产出货季度贡献近 200 亿美元营收，创公司产品最快放量纪录。

第四季度营收指引达到 1261 亿至 1339 亿美元，区间下限仍高于市场预期。公司预计毛利率将在第四季度阶段性触底，2028 财年回升至 72%–73%。

但比财报更值得关注的是管理层变动：董事长 Harvey Jones 表示，董事会无意让黄仁勋复任，已委托猎头寻找正式 CEO，内部与外部候选人均在考察中。

AI 算力需求仍在加速，英伟达甚至进一步上调增长预期，但创始人离场后的管理层交接，也成为这家 AI 巨头新的变量。市场接下来需要同时验证增长能否兑现，以及新 CEO 能否接住英伟达的下一阶段。

tweets.text:
当年以 4 美分 Pass 掉 Solana 种子轮：初级投资人最痛的教训是什么？

Dragonfly 管理合伙人 @hosseeb  在访谈中，复盘了他职业生涯最惨痛的一次错失。

2018 年他刚入行做风投。为了逼自己学习，他不仅给要投的项目写报告，对每一个否决掉的项目，也都会写一份否决备忘录。

那一批被他写过否决备忘录的项目里，就包括当时代币只要 4 美分的 Solana。

Haseeb 回忆，那份备忘录里全是硬核的技术挑刺： “他们在 PPT 里宣称能做到 60 万 TPS，宣称通过 GPU 硬件加速打造超高速链，而我的备忘录一直在逐一挑剔他们每一个细节瑕疵。”

他后来反思，这是年轻投资人最典型的通病：“太字面化地去理解创业者的构想，把投资当成一道家庭作业题，觉得只要把解题步骤写出来、证明他们哪哪都错了，就能得满分。”

“但作为投资人，最糟糕的下场莫过于解题过程全对，但最终结论彻底错了。在数学考试里过程对了还有步骤分；但在投资的世界里，过程全对、结论选错是严格的零分！无论你多聪明、多像个天才，只要选错了，你就是彻底错了。”

挑出别人所有的错误很容易，但这绝不等于你做对了投资。

完整分析，推荐阅读：
https://t.co/9uxDbooss3

在老黄出事前1个月就减持60% $NVDA 仓位，投资大佬段永平真的能未卜先知？

昨晚段永平的 13F 报告一出来，大家都怀疑他提前拿到内幕精准逃顶，毕竟时间线看着太玄乎了。

报告显示，Q3 单季他砍掉 63% 英伟达仓位，三个季度累计减持近七成；紧接着一个多月后，老黄突发辞职，英伟达应声暴跌超 31%。

但如果把持仓报告和他平时在雪球透露的操作策略拼在一起看，其实更像是贯彻了绝对的交易纪律，并没有啥开天眼的操作。

今年 Q1 AI 情绪最热时，段永平曾一路加仓到 1384 万股，把它买成了第三大持仓；但从 Q2 股价继续冲高开始，他就已经开始一直在往外撤了。

你说他完全预见到了老黄会出事那是不可能的；但之所以能撤得这么巧，，是因为他一直在高位卖英伟达的看涨期权（Covered Call）。

股价涨破行权价后，手里的股票被买家自动行权交割了出去，本质上是他觉得 NVDA 短期涨幅透支了基本面，按纪律收下权利金、主动让渡筹码锁定利润，而不是去赌最后一个铜板。

同时，更能说明问题的一点是老黄出事之后的操作。

英伟达暴跌超 31% 之后，段永平不仅没把剩下的 3% 仓位清光，反而在市场最恐慌、期权费暴涨的时候，悄悄开始卖出看跌期权（Sell Put），准备在更低的安全边际把筹码接回来。

他在雪球上也说：“我觉得我买 NVDA 的大部分理由都还在，只是黄不在了。价格上已经都体现出来了，我会很有兴趣看看这个公司能不能走出危机，所以不想急着逃。”

所以看上去的未卜先知，拆开看真的就是很朴素的交易纪律：Q1顺势重仓，Q2+Q3在狂热中被动交割落袋，暴跌后在恐慌里伸手接盘。

顺带一提，13F 里显示，Q3段永平减持的不止英伟达。

谷歌被减持了 41.5%，苹果被减持了 21.76%，微软也小幅减持，甚至清仓了阿里巴巴和稳定币巨头 Circle（CRCL）。

那这笔从狂热科技股里套出来的庞大现金，流向了哪里？

答案是拼多多和特斯拉。

Q3他大幅增持了近 297 万股拼多多，持仓占比拉升到 12.69%，跃居整个组合的第三大重仓；特斯拉被加仓近 70 万股，仓位占比提到 8.42%

一个是现金流极其强悍的下沉消费龙头，另一个是在机器人与航天领域手握排他性壁垒的马斯克体系。

哪有那么多通天神眼，有的只是对纪律常识的绝对遵从。

Gate 回应印度冻结事件：尚未向警方移交任何资产，正协助用户进入正式抗辩程序

针对 ZachXBT 披露的印度警方误冻 Gate 用户账户事件，Gate 今日正式回应称，平台与调查方立场一致，希望案件能够准确、公正解决。

Gate 表示，自收到印度警方请求起，平台优先保障用户权益，已要求警方提供更多证据，而非直接转移资产。目前没有任何资金被移交给警方或报案人。平台在内部审查后认为，印度警方此前提供的材料所显示的资金路径，与 ZachXBT 公开的链上追踪结果存在差异。但由于授权限制，Gate 暂时无法公开相关细节。目前平台正在与印度警方沟通，争取获得同意后向 ZachXBT 及涉事用户同步更多证据，以厘清各方掌握材料不一致的原因。

Gate 同时确认，印度法院已就本案作出裁定。作为合规平台，必须尊重有效的司法命令。现阶段最关键的工作是协助用户尽快进入正式抗辩程序，并已协调当地律师提供支持。平台认为，这是目前解决争议最快、也是最有效的路径。

On-Chain Data Doesn’t Always Match Published Daily Flows

Three reasons:

- Settlement: coins move after the flow is published
- Batching: custodians send set sizes, not one transfer per order
- Internal transfers: moves between a fund's own wallets, with no change in shares

What Pooled Custody Hides

A segregated wallet belongs to one client and can be labelled. An omnibus wallet pools clients' coins and settles transfers between them off-chain - an example being Fidelity Custody.

That's why the 107,000 BTC ($6.87B) Strategy sent to Fidelity Custody is not part of its entity.

#BTC 

Over the past severals weeks, we've covered every single bearish retest of key Weekly levels into new resistances

And over the past two weeks, Bitcoin has accelerated in its downside to the point where it had started losing multiple Weekly levels within a single week

Naturally at some point, the successful bearish retests of Weekly levels into new points of rejection will need to stop

Consistent sell-side capitulation is unsustainable and can't last forever, after all

But at the moment, it doesn't appear that this sequence of bearish retests is over just yet

Bitcoin has recently Weekly Closed below $65700

And Bitcoin is already showcasing initial signs of turning $65700 into new resistance via a bearish retest, in much the same fashion that price did back in June 2026 (light blue circle)

And if Bitcoin wants to avoid additional downside in the direction of $59443, it will need to avoid printing a Weekly Close below the local Weekly support level of ~$63300 (black)

After all - back in June 2026, Bitcoin actually produced a very, very subtle Weekly Close below ~$63300 (blue circle on the zoomed in chart) followed by a bearish retest of it into new resistance to trigger a drop into $59443

Therefore a Weekly Close below ~$63300 followed by a bearish retest of it into new resistance could trigger additional downside continuation

And for Bitcoin to finally end the sequence of these bearish retests, it would need to Weekly Close above ~$65700

Overall, the bearish retests of Weekly levels will continue until at long last proven otherwise ("the trend is your friend") 

But the deeper and deeper Bitcoin sinks in this seller-oriented trend...

The more and more cognisant one needs to be of the inevitability that at some point in the future this series of bearish retests will end and one has to have a plan for that eventuality

$BTC #Bitcoin

#BTC 

Last week, Bitcoin has produced a very decent-sized seller-oriented volume bar, which is a pretty credible candidate for one of Seller Capitulation

And seller volume has certainly experienced hockey-stick, parabolic gaining

Anytime post-seller capitulation, it's always important to watch for whether sellers are finally waning in their strength (seller exhaustion)

Because thus far, seller volume and price reactions have been strongly correlated

Small sell-side volume, small price reaction

Big seller volume, big price reaction

But at some point, there needs to be a decoupling in the influence that seller volume has on price

For example, if at some point in the near future Bitcoin experiences strong above-average seller volume but little price reaction to accompany it, it may be a sign of seller exhaustion

Seller Capitulation is one thing and the volume has recently printed a pretty convincing capitulatory volume bar

Now it's about whether that Capitulation leads to Seller Exhaustion

And if this latest Seller Capitulation doesn't soon lead to weakening sell-side influence on price then the sellers would still remain in control and in that case perhaps more capitulation could be left to endure

Back in 2013 I was living in Spain, watching banks across southern Europe fail one after another. The European debt crisis was in full swing and it got bad enough that I bought a generator and filled the cupboards with tinned food.

Then Cyprus did something no country had done before. Its banks were going under, and instead of rescuing them, the authorities made the depositors pay... anything over €100,000 in your account was swapped for shares in a collapsing bank. They called it a bail-in. People lost their savings overnight.

That was the moment it dawned on me... you don’t actually own the money in your bank account. The bank does. And it can do what it likes with it.

So I went looking for somewhere to keep money that nobody else had a claim on, and that search led me to Bitcoin. I bought my first at around $200.

It started as my escape hatch from a broken banking system and eventually I understood it as the life raft out of the debasement trap.

It’s where the crypto chapter of The Everything Code picks the story up... with a generator and a cupboard full of tinned food.
